title: Make landed CI repeat checks pass under moderately high load

intentCoverage.report:
**Confirmed missing test path.** The examined maintained checks never take collection down the path where `spendRepeat` answers "already spent", so they stay green when collection ignores that answer. A scratch witness shows the fault sends a second rerun request for run 71 after another writer has already spent the landing.

Story and revision: SEED-324#pass-landed-ci-repeat-checks-under-high-load (`.planning/seeds/SEED-324-landed-ci-repeat-checks-under-high-load.md`), plan 599 coverage row C5: "A repeated acceptance and a second dashboard on the machine send nothing more". Checked revision 7bd9f5ccf35af9e5478c579514f34b0860fd6ffc, run in a scratch worktree (detached HEAD, clean before the probe). Node 24.21.0, `setup-native` npm/browser/check all passed, AC power.

Promise and expected behavior: when another writer (a second dashboard on the machine) spends a landing's repeat allowance after this dashboard's pass has made its ledger pre-check, this dashboard must send no rerun request for that landing.

Fault (the caller's suggestion, validated and kept; it is F25 in plan 607): in `dashboard/server/ciFollowUpCollection.ts:90`, `if (!(await spendRepeat(source.id, landing, request))) continue;` was changed to `await spendRepeat(source.id, landing, request);`. Collection then went on to `provider.submit` whatever `spendRepeat` answered. Fixtures and assertions were left unchanged.

Maintained checks examined, with the focused commands the caller supplied:
- `dashboard/backend-tests/intent/landed-ci-automatic-repeat.spec.ts`, `landed-ci-repeat-accepted-request.spec.ts`, `landed-ci-repeat-reconciliation.spec.ts` and `landed-ci-repeat-admission.spec.ts`, 2 workers. Baseline 12 passed. Under the fault 12 passed. After restoring, 12 passed.
- `tests/support/ci-follow-up-ledger.test.mjs` through `bash scripts/test.sh` (quiet on success), including "two independent processes serialize spend" at :70–101. It passed in all three runs. It calls `spendRepeat` directly in worker processes (`tests/fixtures/ci-follow-up-worker.mjs:24`). It never runs `collectCiFollowUps`, so it cannot see what collection does with a `false` answer.
- Why they miss it, from reading the code: in a single-dashboard case, the pass's own pre-check (`ciFollowUpCollection.ts:57–62`, `admitted.request !== undefined` from the ledger read at the start of the pass) already skips a spent landing. `spendRepeat` answers `false` inside collection only when another writer spends between that read and the spend. None of the four specs arranges that.

Independent witness (scratch only, `dashboard/backend-tests/intent/zz-scratch-ic-second-writer.spec.ts`, now deleted):
- Arrangement: `keepRepeatLanding(origin, github, { stage: "eligible receipt", run: 71, seconds: 120, averageSeconds: 100, beside: [heldRequest(waiting run 72)] })`. The fake GitHub answerer was wrapped to hold the server's first `gh` call for run 71. That call was `actions-current-run`, inside `provider.prepare` after the pre-check.
- Steps while that read was held: assert that the run 71 ledger entry is still unspent, then write it through `keepFollowUpEntries` with an accepted request (the other writer's spend). Then release the read, wait with `aWholePass(github, 72, callsAtRelease)`, and assert `rerunRuns(github)` equals `[]`.
- Unfaulted, before the fault: passed, `rerun runs: []`.
- Faulted: failed at `expect(rerunRuns(github), "rerun requests").toEqual([])` with received `[71]`. This confirms the path was reached (the held read came after the pre-check) and the wrong behavior (a rerun request sent for a landing already spent).
- After restoring: passed, `rerun runs: []`.

Restoration: the file was put back from a saved copy by a shell trap. `git diff --quiet -- dashboard/server` was clean. `git status --short` matched the pre-probe state apart from the scratch spec, which was removed with the worktree. The same commands passed after restoring (see above). The scratch worktree was removed with `git worktree remove --force`, and nothing was committed or pushed.

Next proof action: add maintained journey proof for the omitted step. A collecting dashboard that keeps an unspent eligible receipt holds a preparation read of run 71 after its pre-check, another writer spends the landing, the read is released, and after a whole pass the provider has received no rerun request. The witness above is a working shape for it, and the fault above fails it at "rerun requests" with `[71]`.

Matches an existing plan (recognized here, not a new repair decision): plan 607 for SEED-324#close-landed-ci-repeat-check-gaps (at 7bd9f5ccf) already names this fault as F25, plans this case as slice 5 (an eligible-receipt case with another writer's spend during preparation), and lists it as readiness concern P1, "unobserved". This probe observes the F25 half of P1 at the selected revision. Two differences from P1 as written: the read held was `actions-current-run` for run 71, not `actions-attempt-jobs`, and F12 was not probed. Repair and routing stay with the caller.

Costs:
- Test runtime (measured, Playwright's reported totals): focused dashboard specs took 19.7 s at baseline (20.4 s wall), 16.2 s under the fault and 17.2 s after restoring. The scratch witness took 4.2 s at baseline and 4.4 s after restoring; the faulted run failed and its total was not captured. The ledger node test's runtime was not printed (the runner is quiet on success). One-minute load: 1.89→2.52 at baseline, 2.88→3.14 under the fault, 2.88→4.05 after restoring.
- Human effort: unavailable. There is no separate measure; no human took part during the probe.
- Agent effort: unavailable. No separately supported measure of agent tokens or time was available to this run.

- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 246720 ms (measured), from 1794523854451 to 1794524101171 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

- Checked revision: `7bd9f5ccf35af9e5478c579514f34b0860fd6ffc`.
- Decision: compatible gap with the retrospective follow-up. The missing path is slice 5 of plan 607 (fault F25, premise P1) for SEED-324#close-landed-ci-repeat-check-gaps, queued first. Plan 607's P1 now records this observation (F25 settled, F12 open) and its readiness was reassessed as not ready; one queue entry is kept.
- Evidence: the witness above; no delivered product defect is claimed (the fault is a scratch edit).
